citation.title: A Multi-Grid, Single-Mesh Online Learning Framework for Stress-Constrained Topology Optimization Based on Isogeometric Formulation

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Online learning reduces the number of isogeometric analyses and total runtime while producing designs described as comparable to the ground-truth optimization.
claim.key_phrase: reducing the total computational time by about 20%
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Table 1 reports a speed-up of 1.23; the results text also says evaluations fall from 210 to 150 and total time falls by about 20%.
claim.alternatives: For a 207 × 102 control-point grid, reported speed-up is 1.78× (Table 5).

baseline.hardware_classical: Windows 10 Pro, Intel i7-11700 CPU, 16 GB RAM, NVIDIA RTX 3060 GPU (12 GB)
baseline.hardware_ml: Windows 10 Pro, Intel i7-11700 CPU, 16 GB RAM, NVIDIA RTX 3060 GPU (12 GB)
baseline.problem_size: 103 × 52 control points in main cases; additional 63 × 48 and 207 × 102 cases
baseline.classical_iterations: Ground-truth TO-IGA 210 iterations; online approach uses 150 IGA evaluations in main case
baseline.classical_time: Table 1; online method total 20% less time, exact paired times not transcribed here
baseline.ml_time: Table 1; online method total 20% less time, exact paired times not transcribed here
baseline.training_time: not stated separately; training/tuning 150 epochs within online process (Section 5)
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated separately; data collected from prior optimization iterations (Section 5)
baseline.quality_metric: objective/volume fraction and maximum von Mises stress; stress constraint satisfaction
baseline.quality_gap: Results described as comparable to ground-truth TO-IGA; relative error about 0.1% is discussed (Section 5)

R1.evidence: Section 5 and Tables 1–2 report comparable designs and volume/stress outcomes alongside reduced analyses and runtime; matching is not described in further detail.

R2.evidence: Section 5 does not establish an inefficient classical solver, unjustified hardware mismatch, or unnecessary fixed iteration count; both methods use the stated machine.

R3.evidence: The model learns online from the current optimization trajectory; no offline training or separate data-generation campaign is described (Sections 1 and 5).

R4.evidence: Section 5 reports IGA-computed stress and volume outcomes for returned designs, but does not count failed or infeasible designs.

reporting.n_test_cases: Two main stress-constrained examples plus two resolution variants
